item.title: Infinitary real-valued logic and a refinement of the Kochen-Specker theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.05656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For nearly sixty years, refinements of the Bell-Kochen-Specker theorem have concentrated on finite configurations, combinatorics and robustness; once a configuration is fixed, contextuality is witnessed by the inconsistency of a finite family of Boolean constraints. We study the theorem instead with infinitary real-valued logic and a model existence game. We axiomatize, in real-valued $L_{\omega_1\omega}$, the lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space together with a quantum probability measure. In the standard models the theory recovers Gleason's theorem. Once the axiom that the measure is $\{0,1\}$-valued is adjoined, the theory has no models, standard or nonstandard, although every finite set of its axioms has one; a model existence game converts this infinitary inconsistency into finite inconsistent sets of interval commitments on the values of sentences. Over the standard models, the subsets of $[0,1]$ that formulas define through the values of the measure are exactly the $\sigma$-projective sets, the members of the least class containing the Borel sets and closed under complements, countable unions and projections along $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$; the classification is proved in ZFC. For a specified strategy in the game, the plays that complete the parity argument for the eighteen-ray configuration of Cabello, Estebaranz and Garc\'ia-Alcaine record the geometric identities between the occurrences of a ray in different contexts, and the use that the measure makes of them. Probabilities are tracked up to rational tolerances, and $\sigma$-additivity along a named basis selects the four-dimensional block in which the argument takes place. The refinement is thus not a smaller Kochen-Specker set but a finer analysis of the logical form of the obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Aubone, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Rule extensions of the implication--negation fragment of intuitionistic logic
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an algebraic study of extensions of the implication--negation fragment $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ of intuitionistic propositional logic. Such extensions by inference rules correspond to subquasivarieties of the variety $\var{Ho}$ of Hilbert algebras with zero. We describe the lattice of such extensions of $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ by means of its generators: it is isomorphic to the lattice of upsets of a countable poset, and in particular it is completely distributive. Consequently, $\var{Ho}$ is not Q-universal, in contrast to several other varieties related to $\mathrm{IPC}$. Nevertheless, this lattice is very complex: at each suitably defined height it has intervals containing continuum many quasivarieties which are not varieties. To the best of our knowledge $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ is the only natural fragment of intuitionistic logic known to combine a completely distributive lattice of extensions with continuum many non-axiomatic extensions.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kowalski, Katarzyna S{\l}omczy\'nska

item.title: The Cone Fixing the Reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{2n}(x)}
item.description: arXiv:2611.06032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a cone of reals $x$, the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}$ are precisely the reals in $Q_3$, or equivalently, the set of reals in $M_1$, the minimal proper class mouse with a Woodin cardinal. We show that if $z$ is any real coding $M_1|\delta^{+M_1}$, then $z$ is the base of such a cone (so $M_1^{\#}$ is such a base). We also establish a kind of optimality for this result, by identifying a real $x$ such that $M_1\subseteq L[x]$ but $\mathbb{R}\cap\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}\not\subseteq M_1$, although there is a base for the cone in a generic extension of $L[x]$. We prove analogous results for $M_{2n}(x)$ for all $n$, with the optimality result holding for all $n$.
item.dc:creator: Farmer Schlutzenberg, Connor Watson

item.title: A weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set under $\frak{p} = \frak{c}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$, Cantor space contains a weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set. This answers the consistency question of de Oliveira Rodrigues, dos Santos Ronchim, and Szeptycki. The hypothesis $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$ is compatible with the failure of the continuum hypothesis. The construction combines the finite-unions form of Hindman's theorem with Bell's characterization of $\mathfrak p$ in terms of $\sigma$-centered forcing. The increasing enumerations of the infinite members of the constructed space form an unbounded family under eventual domination. This makes the countable set of finite subsets of $\omega$ a witness to the failure of the $\lambda$-property.
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Osipov, Anton E. Lipin

item.title: Definably isometric cuboids over Hensel minimal fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.06413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, over a valued field $K$ with $1$-h-minimal theory $\operatorname{Th}(K)$, two Cartesian products of balls must be equal up to translation and coordinate permutation in order for there to exist a definable surjective isometry between them. For this purpose, we introduce a notion of relative dimension for cuboids in $K^n$ that is computed combinatorially and relates to the notion of dimension for definable sets in Hensel minimal theories when $K$ has infinite residue field.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Fortmann

item.title: Escaping and generics over ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.06439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relation between the existence of escaping (or hyperimmune) functions and weak 1-genericity using computability over ideals. We prove in particular the existence of an $\mathcal{I}$-escaping function which does not $\mathcal{I}$-compute any weakly $\mathcal{I}$-generic set whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is a countable Turing ideal closed under the existence of diagonally non-computable functions.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Bienvenu, Noam Greenberg, Ludovic Patey, Dan Turetsky

item.title: The group of strong automorphisms of the differential field of transseries
item.description: arXiv:2611.06520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the group of strongly additive automorphisms of the differential field $\mathbb T$ of transseries as a non-trivial semidirect product. We show that this group is torsion-free and has trivial center, and that many naturally arising differential subfields of $\mathbb T$ are definably closed in $\mathbb T$.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Aschenbrenner, Lou van den Dries, Joris van der Hoeven

item.title: The Logic of Emergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.06641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ``Emergence'' refers to the fact that different mathematical languages and theories seem to be required to describe scientific theories that operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Highly circumscribed, special cases of emergence have been investigated using many different formal tools, including coarse-graining (over space and / or time), renormalization, dimension reduction, broken symmetry, and various formulations of causality. Here we extend the mathematics of model theory to unify and extend these earlier investigations. As a preliminary application of our framework, we investigate canonical examples of emergence, including the emergence of genetics from chemistry, of psychology from neurobiology, and of different forms of collective behavior from the laws governing their constituent parts. By exploiting the power of model theory we also uncover many aspects of emergence that were previously obscured. In particular, we uncover some of the rich hierarchical structure that relates different scientific fields. For example, we show that scientific fields can be related via a collection of multiple partial orders, all defined over the same set. On the other hand, under an alternative relation among scientific fields, one which allows cycles, we show that it is possible that the set of all of scientific fields must collapse into a single scientific field. Going forward, these investigations point to the formal tools that might need to be developed in order to arrive at a deeper understanding of this emergent hierarchy of scientific reality.
item.dc:creator: David H. Wolpert, David C. Krakauer

item.title: Diophantine definability from addition and divisibility over rings of $S$-integers
item.description: arXiv:2611.05687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $K$ containing the archimedean places, and let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ denote the ring of $S$-integers of $K$. We prove that multiplication is positive-existentially definable in $(\mathcal{O}_{K,S},0,1,+,\mid)$ if and only if the unit group $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}^\times$ is infinite. This extends a 1977 theorem of Lipshitz for rings of integers to rings of $S$-integers. One of the key ingredients is a uniform bound for unit equations due to Evertse, Schlickewei and Schmidt, which we use to recover multiplication on the unit group.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Mart\'inez-Ranero

item.title: An Engineering Reading of the Bounded Halting Problem and Observable Properties of a Universal Machine
item.description: arXiv:2611.06303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The halting problem asks whether a program eventually halts, with unrestricted resources. Engineering systems instead certify bounded halting: given a program, an input, and a step budget T, decide whether the program halts within T steps. This paper studies two of its uses. First, it defines an exact finite-budget problem, placing the simulated program and the checker on the same unit-cost timescale, so the checker can be embedded in an adversarial program. A diagonal argument with explicit additive overhead shows that no fixed deterministic checker decides every instance within any fixed fraction of T below one, for large T. In the nondeterministic case, T bounds the branch depth allowed for a stable observable decision. Second, bounded-halting instances give adversarial tests for finitary universality, since a universal model must support arbitrary finite computations as T grows. The tests check resource growth with T, the absence of a fixed deliberation bound, and later access to intermediate data. They separate a fixed model with extendable external resources, a model family that grows with T, and a larger system built around a fixed component. For machine-learning systems, this identifies the resource growth a universality claim assumes and whether it fails for deployed models.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: S. Salishev, CYBERNETICS AND PHYSICS, VOL. 15, NO. 2, 2026, 234-242
item.dc:creator: Sergey Salishev

item.title: Monadically Dependent Graph Classes Have Almost Bounded Merge-Width
item.description: arXiv:2611.06804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A graph class $\mathcal{C}$ is monadically dependent if one cannot interpret all graphs in vertex-colored graphs from $\mathcal{C}$ using a fixed formula of first-order logic. We prove that every monadically dependent graph class has almost bounded merge-width, thereby confirming a conjecture of the first and the last author [STOC '25]. Our proof is algorithmic and the witnessing decompositions in the form of merge sequences can be computed in nearly-cubic time. This is a step towards the proof of fixed-parameter tractability of model checking first-order logic on monadically dependent graph classes, which is achieved in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Jan Dreier, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: Combining Determinism and Indeterminism
item.description: arXiv:2009.03996v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Our goal is to construct mathematical operations that combine indeterminism measured from quantum randomness with computational determinism so that non-mechanistic behavior is preserved in the computation. Formally, some results about operations applied to computably enumerable (c.e.) and bi-immune sets are proven here, where the objective is for the operations to preserve bi-immunity. While developing rearrangement operations on the natural numbers, we discovered that the bi-immune rearrangements generate an uncountable subgroup of the infinite symmetric group (Sym$(\mathbb{N})$) on the natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$. This new uncountable subgroup is called the bi-immune symmetric group. We show that the bi-immune symmetric group contains the finitary symmetric group on the natural numbers, and consequently is highly transitive. Furthermore, the bi-immune symmetric group is dense in Sym$(\mathbb{N})$ with respect to the pointwise convergence topology. The complete structure of the bi-immune symmetric group and its subgroups generated by one or more bi-immune rearrangements is unknown.
item.dc:creator: Michael Stephen Fiske

item.title: Forcing with Symmetric Systems of Models of Two Types
item.description: arXiv:2210.12741v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a general method for forcing on $\omega_2$ and $\omega_3$ with finite conditions, while preserving all cardinals and some fragments of $\mathrm{GCH}$. This method is based on the technique of forcing with finite symmetric systems of elementary submodels, and improves earlier versions of this forcing by including models of two types. We will present several applications of the pure side condition forcing and variants thereof, by adding a Kurepa tree on $\omega_2$, a club subset of $\omega_2$ that avoids infinite sets from the ground model, a function bounding every canonical function below $\omega_3$ on a club, and a simplified $(\omega_2,1)$-morass.
item.dc:creator: Curial Gallart

item.title: More on expressibility of satisfiability in submodels and extensions
item.description: arXiv:2605.02725v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study expressibility in infinitary languages of the modal operators associated with satisfiability of sentences of these languages in submodels and extensions of models. We give a syntactic criterion for expressibility in finitary predicate languages, show that in many cases infinitary languages are closed under the operator associated with submodels, and that this is so in any language with a purely monadic signature. Finally, we prove that in finitary or strongly compact languages, the operator associated with extensions, though can be inexpressible by a single sentence, is always expressible by a universal theory, in striking contrast with the submodel case.
item.dc:creator: Nikolai L. Poliakov, Denis I. Saveliev

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.22205v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the third paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. Here we study simplicity through two countable structures with simple unstable theories: the Rado graph, and the symplectic space of labels of Pauli strings of finite support, in which addition records the products of the strings and the symplectic form records their commutation. In the second structure, forking characterizes the logical errors of stabilizer codes: an error undetectable by the checks of a code is logical exactly when its type over the stabilizer labels and a complete set of logical-operator labels forks over the stabilizer labels, and the independence theorem becomes a rule for gluing syndromes. A two-valued relation between countable sets of labels defines a diagonal bipartite observable, whose real-valued theory describes Alice's probability mixtures of labels and their expected responses at Bob's probes. Mixing changes the classification: if the relation has the independence property, this theory has the tree property of the second kind. For the observable of the symplectic form, actual mixtures of checks witness this property for the response itself; for the observable of the Rado graph, every array that witnesses it for a quantifier-free formula in Bob's probe contains idealized preparations, which lie outside the original structure.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~{n}ez, Jos\'{e} Iovino

item.title: Well begun is half done: the computation of Eulerian paths
item.description: arXiv:2611.00818v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the uniform computational strength of finding (one-way or two-way, directed or undirected) Eulerian paths in countable graphs. In the one-way case, for both directed and undirected graphs, this problem is Weihrauch-equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}\times\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ is the jump of closed choice on the natural numbers. This refines the proof-theoretic strength of the existence of a one-way Eulerian path given by the reverse mathematics framework. The $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ component comes entirely from the difficulty of choosing a starting vertex: with a valid start prescribed, the problem is equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}$, which also characterizes the degree of the two-way directed/undirected Eulerian path problem. We also study the complexity of orienting the edges of a graph while preserving the existence of a one-way/two-way Eulerian path. In the one-way case, this problem is not computable, and we prove that $\mathsf{lim}_2<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{OrientEP}<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{2}'\sqcap\mathsf{Sort}_2$ and $\mathsf{OrientEP}\not\le_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$. On the other hand, valid orientations are uniformly computable for two-way paths and for one-way paths with a prescribed valid starting vertex.
item.dc:creator: Manlio Valenti

item.title: Existentially defining valuations in function fields over large fields
item.description: arXiv:2512.04896v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a large field such that $K[\sqrt{-1}]$ is not algebraically closed and $F/K$ a function field in one variable. Extending techniques and results from earlier work with Becher and Dittmann, we show that every valuation ring on $F$ containing $K$ is existentially definable in the language of rings with parameters from $F$. As a consequence, using a known reduction technique, we obtain the undecidability of the existential theory of $F$ in the language of rings with appropriately chosen parameters.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Daans

item.title: $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-networks, $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizability, and local HCP-finiteness
item.description: arXiv:2609.30317v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal I$ be an admissible ideal on $\mathbb N$. Zhou, Liu, Liu, and Lin asked whether every regular space with a $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizable. The answer is affirmative for every admissible ideal. The proof rests on a local countability theorem. If $y_n\to_{\mathcal I}x$ and $\{n\mid y_n\ne x\}\in\mathcal I^+$, then every point-discrete family of $\mathcal I$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is countable. In a $T_1$ space, this applies in particular to every HCP family. If no $\mathcal I$-convergent sequence to $x$ has $\mathcal I$-positive support away from $x$, then $\{x\}$ is an $\mathcal I$-sequential neighborhood. It follows that every space with a $\sigma$-point-discrete $\mathcal I$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal I$-$snf$-countable. This conclusion, together with the characterization theorems of Ge and of Zhou, Liu, Liu, and Lin, settles Problem 5.2. The countability bound cannot in general be strengthened to finiteness. A countable Rudin--Keisler antichain of free ultrafilters gives an admissible ideal for which local HCP-finiteness fails. Every $P^{-}$ ideal has local HCP-finiteness. Preservation theorems for Fubini products, heterogeneous Fubini sums under cross-row Kat\v{e}tov absorption, and suitable increasing unions extend local HCP-finiteness beyond the $P^{-}$ class. They apply to the finite Fubini powers of $\mathrm{Fin}$, Kat\v{e}tov's first limit-stage ideal $\mathrm{Fin}^{\omega}$ and its finite successors, the tree-derived rank-$\omega$ ideal $\mathcal H_{<\omega}$, and the inductive-limit ideal $\mathrm{Fin}_{\omega}$. Every listed example other than $\mathrm{Fin}$ fails $P^{-}$.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu
